text:
eva: hey! first-day question  I'm trying to switch to the dev cluster but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows a context `dev-team-prodlike` and `kubectl get pods -n eva-dev` errors with Forbidden. I followed the onboarding doc but maybe missed a step.

mason: welcome! what did you run to generate your kubeconfig? (aws sso / gcloud / k8s certs?)

eva: aws sso. I did `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` then `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev -r us-east-1 --profile redwood-onboard`. kubeconfig merged something that references an arn role.

mason: check `kubectl config view --raw | sed -n '/users:/,$p'` and see the `exec` command. If it's `aws eks get-token` that's normal. If the ARN in the context is a role you don't have, infra needs to bind you a RoleBinding in the namespace you want.

eva: pasted exec snippet: `command: aws args: ["eks","get-token","--cluster-name","redwood-dev","--region","us-east-1","--profile","redwood-onboard"] env: [{name: AWS_PROFILE, value: redwood-onboard}]`

samir: for new hires we usually give a namespace-scoped role called `onboard-edit`. File an access request and include `namespace=eva-dev` and mention you only need kubectl edit/get/list for iteration. That saves granting cluster-wide perms.

eva: where's the access form? I only see the infra slackbot command in another channel.

mason: https://redwood.example.com/access -> choose "Kubernetes namespace access". If you need a quick workaround, infra can create a temporary ServiceAccount and give you a kubeconfig that impersonates it, but that requires a support ticket.

eva: I tried `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n eva-dev` and got "no". I'll submit the form.

infra-bot: access request created by eva at 1961002355  request id K-9921. Assigned to infra oncall. ETA ~1.5h.

eva: thx. another tiny Q: any recommended local alias for jumping namespaces? I keep typing `-n` wrong.

mason: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=eva-dev` sets your default ns for the context. I also use `k -n` alias for `kubectl -n`.

samir: once infra approves you'll be able to `kubectl get pods -n eva-dev`. if you need portforwards let infra know so they don't block the SA.

eva: update: infra approved. did `aws sso login` again then `kubectl get pods -n eva-dev` works now. leaving note: re-run `aws sso login` after access was granted so the token picks up the role mapping. cheers!
